section_summary.extract_value: This section explores the relationship between humor and intelligence, citing several studies. Koppel and Sechrest (1970) found a correlation of r = .23 between intelligence and humor funniness. Howrigan and MacDonald (2008) reported a correlation of r = .29 between a compound humor production measure and intelligence. Greengross and Miller (2011) observed correlations of r = .24 with fluid intelligence and r = .31 with verbal intelligence for humor production. Greengross et al. (2012) further found a correlation of r = .39 between humor production and verbal intelligence in university students, but not in a sample of 31 comedians.
